question.text: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one end is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. The same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about a diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be ______.

solution.text:
Moment of inertia of rod rotating about an axis passing through one end is I1=ml23     ⋯1 

Moment of inertia of ring rotating about one of its diameters is I2=mR22.

Since the rod is bent into a ring, the circumference of the ring and the length of the rod are equal, l=2πR

Then, I2=mR22=ml28π2 

Thus, the ratio I1I2=8π23, so x=8.
